q: Which part of a roadway must be kept open at all times for firefighting?
n: A fire lane is the part of a roadway or area that must be kept clear at all times for fire apparatus. Source: RA 9514 (Fire Code) RIRR 2019, Sec. 3 (definitions).

q: What is any condition that increases fire risk or hinders firefighting?
n: A fire hazard is any condition or act that increases the risk of fire or hinders firefighting. Source: RA 9514 RIRR 2019, Sec. 3.

q: What is the minimum width of any means of egress?
n: The width of any means of egress shall be at least 915 mm, unless an occupancy chapter specifies otherwise. Source: RA 9514 RIRR 2019, Sec. 10.2.5.1 F.

q: What is the minimum clear distance in mm of fire escape stairs between rails?
n: Fire escape stairs need at least 600 mm clear width between rails. Source: RA 9514 RIRR 2019, Sec. 10.2.5.10, Table 6.

q: What is the maximum riser height of fire escape stairs in cm?
n: Fire escape stairs have a maximum rise of 230 mm (23 cm). Source: RA 9514 RIRR 2019, Sec. 10.2.5.10, Table 6.

q: What is the minimum tread width of fire escape stairs in cm?
n: The minimum tread of a fire escape stair, excluding nosing, is 230 mm (23 cm). Source: RA 9514 RIRR 2019, Sec. 10.2.5.10, Table 6.

q: What is the minimum and maximum height of railings at the fire escape stairs?
n: Fire escape handrails must be on both sides, at least 760 mm and at most 1,070 mm high (76–107 cm). Source: RA 9514 RIRR 2019, Sec. 10.2.5.10.

q: What device is used on fire exit doors?
n: Fire exit doors use panic hardware, horizontal bars that release the latch when pushed. Source: RA 9514 RIRR 2019, Sec. 3 (Panic Hardware) and Sec. 10.2.5.2.

q: What is a continuous, unobstructed route of exit from any point in a building?
n: A means of egress is a continuous, unobstructed route of exit from any point in a building to a public way. It has three parts: exit access, exit and exit discharge. Source: RA 9514 RIRR 2019, Sec. 3; NFPA 101.

q: Which is NOT a standard fire-resistance rating?
n: Standard fire-resistance ratings run up to 4 hours (1, 2, 3, 4). A 5-hour rating is not standard. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VII, Table VII.1; ASTM E119.

q: Window width for fire exit?
n: Windows giving access to fire escape stairs must have a clear opening of at least 762 × 914 mm (double-hung). Of the choices, 800 mm is the nearest width that satisfies the 762 mm minimum. Source: RA 9514 RIRR 2019, Sec. 10.2.5.10, Table 6.

q: Fire exit door should open?
n: Exit doors must be openable from the egress side at all times without keys or special knowledge while the building is occupied. Source: RA 9514 RIRR 2019, Sec. 10.2.5.2.

q: What material blocks a concealed space through which fire could spread?
n: A firestop (fire blocking) is material that seals a concealed space, such as a wall cavity or joist space, so fire cannot spread through it. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VII; RA 9514 RIRR 2019.

q: Under RA 9514, what is a building unsafe in case of fire called?
n: RA 9514 defines a fire trap as a building unsafe in case of fire because it will burn easily or lacks adequate exits or fire escapes. Source: RA 9514, Sec. 3.

q: Under RA 9514, any act that removes or neutralizes a fire hazard is:
n: Under RA 9514, abatement is any act that removes or neutralizes a fire hazard. Source: RA 9514, Sec. 3.

q: Minimum width of fire exit door:
n: Exit doors must give at least 900 mm clear width. The width lets occupants and wheelchairs pass through quickly during evacuation. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule XII, Sec. 1207.

q: Who implements the Fire Code?
o: The Office of the Building Official
n: RA 9514 vests enforcement of the Fire Code in the Chief, Bureau of Fire Protection, under the DILG. Source: RA 9514 (Fire Code of 2008), Sec. 5.

q: Which body does NOT enforce the Fire Code in construction?
n: The Fire Code is enforced by the BFP, with the OBO and LGU checking fire safety in permits. The PRBOA regulates the architecture profession only. Source: RA 9514, Sec. 5; RA 9266, Sec. 7.

q: What is the time a material can withstand a standard fire test?
n: The fire resistance rating is the time, in hours, a material or assembly withstands a standard fire test. Source: RA 9514 RIRR 2019, Sec. 3; ASTM E119.

q: Which is the Fire Code law?
n: RA 9514 is the Fire Code of the Philippines of 2008. It replaced PD 1185 and is enforced by the Bureau of Fire Protection under its 2019 Revised IRR. Source: RA 9514.

q: Which law is the National Plumbing Code?
n: RA 1378 (1955) is the Plumbing Law, the basis of the National Plumbing Code of the Philippines. Source: RA 1378; National Plumbing Code (1999 revision).

q: Structural code law:
n: The structural code is the National Structural Code of the Philippines (NSCP), 2015 edition (Vol. 1), issued by ASEP and referred to by PD 1096. Source: NSCP 2015 (ASEP); NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VI.

q: Which law is the National Building Code?
n: PD 1096 (1977) is the National Building Code of the Philippines. It governs the design, construction, use and maintenance of buildings and is administered by the DPWH and LGU Building Officials. Source: PD 1096.

q: Which law covers economic and socialized housing standards?
n: BP 220 (1982) covers economic and socialized housing standards. BP 220 allows smaller lots and lower standards than PD 957, so housing stays affordable to low-income families. Source: BP 220 and its Revised IRR.

q: Which is the Forestry Code of the Philippines?
n: PD 705 (1975) is the Revised Forestry Code of the Philippines. PD 705 governs the classification, management and use of forest lands and timber resources. Source: PD 705.

q: Which is the PRC Modernization Act of 2000?
n: RA 8981 is the PRC Modernization Act of 2000. RA 8981 strengthened the PRC's powers to regulate the professions and their Boards. Source: RA 8981.

q: RA 9285 is the:
n: RA 9285 is the Alternative Dispute Resolution Act of 2004. It encourages settling disputes through mediation, arbitration and other alternatives to court litigation. Source: RA 9285.

q: What government agency implements the provision of RA 9285?
n: Under RA 9285, construction disputes go to the Construction Industry Arbitration Commission (CIAC), which has original and exclusive jurisdiction under EO 1008. Source: RA 9285, Sec. 34–35; EO 1008.

q: Which law sets technical standards for economic and socialized housing in rural and urban areas?
n: BP 220 sets technical standards for economic and socialized housing in both urban and rural areas. Source: BP 220, Sec. 1–2.

q: With a 450 mm toilet seat, about how high from the floor is the top of the grab bar beside an accessible water closet?
n: The 2024 IRR puts the top of the grab bar 300 mm above the seat. With a 450 mm seat, it is 450 + 300 = 750 mm from the floor. Source: BP 344 IRR (2024 amendment), accessible toilet provisions.

q: Under the 2024 BP 344 IRR, what is the minimum wheelchair turning space?
n: The 2024 BP 344 IRR raised the minimum wheelchair turning space to 1.80 × 1.80 m, from 1.50 m. Source: BP 344 IRR (2024 amendment).

q: What are the minimum inside dimensions of an accessible elevator car?
n: An accessible elevator car must be at least 1.20 m wide and 1.40 m deep inside, with a 900 mm door. Source: BP 344 IRR (2024 amendment), elevator provisions.

q: At most how far from the main entrance should an accessible elevator be?
n: An accessible elevator should be no more than 30 m from the building's main entrance. Source: BP 344 IRR, Rule II, elevators.

q: At what height range should light switches be for PWDs?
n: Light switches and controls for PWDs should be 0.90–1.20 m above the floor. Source: BP 344 IRR (2024 amendment), switches and controls.

q: A central refuge is required when the carriageway to be crossed is wider than:
n: A central refuge island is required where the carriageway to be crossed is wider than 10 m (or has four or more lanes). Source: BP 344 IRR, Rule II, crossings.
